title.zh: 卷三十 漢臣傳第十八: 蘇逢吉 史弘肇 楊邠 王章 劉銖 李業 聶文進 後贊 郭允明
title.en: Volume 30 Later Han Biographies 10: Su Fengji, Shi Hongzhao, Yang Bin, Wang Zhang, Liu Zhu, Li Ye, Nie Wenjin, Hou Zan, Guo Yunming
title.raw: 卷三十 漢臣傳第十八: 蘇逢吉 史弘肇 楊邠 王章 劉銖 李業 聶文進 後贊 郭允明 Volume 30 Later Han Biographies 10: Su Fengji, Shi Hongzhao, Yang Bin, Wang Zhang, Liu Zhu, Li Ye, Nie Wenjin, Hou Zan, Guo Yunming

sentences.zh: 蘇逢吉

translations.literal: Su Fengji
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji

sentences.zh: 蘇逢吉，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Su Fengji was a native of Chang’an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji came from Chang’an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖鎮河東，父悅為高祖從事，逢吉常代悅作奏記，悅乃言之高祖。

translations.literal: When the Han High Ancestor governed Hedong, Fengji’s father Yue served as the High Ancestor’s staff officer. Fengji often drafted memorials in Yue’s place, and Yue spoke of him to the High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: While the Han High Ancestor held Hedong, Fengji’s father Yue served on his staff. Fengji often wrote memorials for Yue, and Yue commended him to the High Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 高祖召見逢吉，精神爽秀，憐之，乃以為節度判官。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor summoned Fengji for an audience. He was bright and handsome in bearing; the High Ancestor took pity on him and made him military governor’s aide.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor received Fengji and found him keen-eyed and fine in bearing. He took a liking to him and made him the military governor’s aide.

sentences.zh: 高祖性素剛嚴，賓佐稀得請見，逢吉獨入，終日侍立高祖書閣中。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor’s nature was always stern and severe; his staff seldom gained audience. Fengji alone entered and spent whole days standing attendance in the High Ancestor’s study pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor was stern by nature; his staff rarely saw him. Fengji alone went in and stood all day in the High Ancestor’s study.

sentences.zh: 兩使文簿盈積，莫敢通，逢吉輒取內之懷中，伺高祖色可犯時以進之，高祖多以為可，以故甚愛之。

translations.literal: Memorials from the two commissioners piled up; none dared pass them through. Fengji would take them into his robes and, watching for moments when the High Ancestor’s expression permitted intrusion, present them. The High Ancestor mostly approved—hence his great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials from the two commissioners stacked up; no one dared forward them. Fengji tucked them in his robe and, when the High Ancestor’s face looked passable, slipped them in. The High Ancestor usually assented—and came to love him for it.

sentences.zh: 然逢吉為人貪詐無行，喜為殺戮。

translations.literal: Yet Fengji as a man was greedy, deceitful, and without rectitude, delighting in killing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Fengji was greedy, treacherous, and without principle—and he loved blood.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗以生日遣逢吉疏理獄囚以祈福，謂之「靜獄。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor once on his birthday dispatched Fengji to review and clear the prison inmates to pray for blessing—calling it “Quieting the Prisons.
translations.idiomatic: On his birthday the High Ancestor sent Fengji to sort the prisons and clear the inmates for a blessing—calling it “Quieting the Prisons.

sentences.zh: 」逢吉入獄中閱囚，無輕重曲直悉殺之，以報曰：「獄靜矣。」

translations.literal: ” Fengji entered the prison to review the inmates and, regardless of seriousness or rightness, killed them all, then reported: “The prison is quiet.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Fengji went through the cells and killed every prisoner, light or heavy, guilty or not, then reported: “The prisons are quiet.”

sentences.zh: 高祖建號，拜逢吉中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor established his regnal title, Fengji was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Co-signer of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor took the throne, Fengji became Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Co-signer of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 是時，制度草創，朝廷大事皆出逢吉，逢吉以為己任。

translations.literal: At that time institutions were newly founded; major court affairs all issued from Fengji, and Fengji took them as his own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Institutions were still being invented; every great matter ran through Fengji, and he treated the realm as his charge.

sentences.zh: 然素不學問，隨事裁決，出其意見，是故漢世尤無法度，而不施德政，民莫有所稱焉。

translations.literal: Yet he had never studied; he decided matters as they arose from his own opinions—thus the Han era was especially without law, and without benevolent governance, so the people had nothing by which to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: He had never studied and ruled by whim—so Han had less law than ever, less mercy, and the people had nothing good to say of him.

sentences.zh: 高祖既定京師，逢吉與蘇禹珪同在中書，除吏多違舊制。

translations.literal: After the High Ancestor had secured the capital, Fengji and Su Yugui both served in the Secretariat; appointments often violated old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Once the capital was settled, Fengji and Su Yugui shared the Secretariat—and appointments broke old rules at every turn.

sentences.zh: 逢吉尤納貨賂，市權鬻官，謗者喧嘩。

translations.literal: Fengji especially took bribes, trafficking in power and selling offices—complainers clamored.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji above all took bribes, sold offices, and traded in power—complaint became a din.

sentences.zh: 然高祖方倚信二人，故莫敢有告者。

translations.literal: But the High Ancestor then relied on and trusted the two men, so none dared report them.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor still leaned on the two men, and no one dared accuse them.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔李永吉初朝京師，逢吉以永吉故秦王從嚴子，家世王侯，當有奇貨，使人告永吉，許以一州，而求其先王玉帶，永吉以無為解，逢吉乃使人市一玉帶，直數千緡，責永吉償之；

translations.literal: When Li Yongji of Fengxiang first came to court in the capital, Fengji thought that Yongji, being a son of the former Prince of Qin Congyan, came from generations of kings and marquises and ought to possess rare treasures. He had someone inform Yongji, promising a prefecture in exchange, and demand the jade belt of Yongji’s forebear king. Yongji pleaded he did not have it. Fengji then had someone buy a jade belt worth several thousand strings of cash and billed Yongji for it;
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yongji of Fengxiang first came to court, Fengji reckoned that as a son of the former Prince of Qin Congyan, from a line of kings and marquises, he must hold rare treasure. He sent word promising a prefecture for the ancestral jade belt. Yongji said he had none. Fengji bought a belt for several thousand strings of cash and billed Yongji for it;

sentences.zh: 前客省使王筠自晉末使楚，至是還，逢吉意筠得楚王重賂，遣人求之，許以一州，筠怏怏，以其橐裝之半獻之。

translations.literal: The former Guest Liaison Commissioner Wang Jun had been sent to Chu from the end of Jin; now he returned. Fengji suspected Jun had received heavy bribes from the King of Chu and sent men to demand them, promising a prefecture. Jun was resentful and presented half his baggage as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, once envoy to Chu in Jin’s last days, had now returned. Fengji suspected heavy bribes from the King of Chu and demanded them, again promising a prefecture. Jun, sullen, gave up half his baggage.

sentences.zh: 而皆不得州。

translations.literal: Yet neither received a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Neither man got his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 晉相李崧從契丹以北，高祖入京師，以崧第賜逢吉，而崧別有田宅在西京，逢吉遂皆取之。

translations.literal: The Jin chancellor Li Song followed the Khitan north. When the High Ancestor entered the capital, he gave Song’s mansion to Fengji; Song also had fields and dwellings separately in the Western Capital—Fengji took those too.
translations.idiomatic: Jin chancellor Li Song had gone north with the Khitan. When the High Ancestor entered the capital he gave Song’s mansion to Fengji—and took Song’s fields and houses in the Western Capital as well.

sentences.zh: 崧自北還，因以宅券獻逢吉，逢吉不悅，而崧子弟數出怨言。

translations.literal: When Song returned from the north he therefore presented the deed of the mansion to Fengji. Fengji was displeased, and Song’s sons and younger brothers repeatedly uttered resentful words.
translations.idiomatic: Song returned from the north and handed over the deed. Fengji was displeased; Song’s sons and brothers muttered their grievances.

sentences.zh: 其後，逢吉乃誘人告崧與弟嶼、義等，下獄，崧款自誣伏：「與家僮二十人，謀因高祖山陵為亂。

translations.literal: Afterward Fengji had someone induced to report Song and his brothers Yu and Yi. They were imprisoned. Song in confession falsely implicated himself: “With twenty household slaves I plotted to use the High Ancestor’s mountain tomb to raise disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji then had Song and his brothers Yu and Yi denounced and thrown into prison. Song confessed under torture: “With twenty household slaves I meant to stir trouble at the High Ancestor’s tomb.

sentences.zh: 」獄上中書，逢吉改「二十人」為「五十人」，遂族崧家。

translations.literal: ” The case went up to the Secretariat; Fengji changed “twenty men” to “fifty men” and then exterminated Song’s clan.
translations.idiomatic: ” The file reached the Secretariat; Fengji changed “twenty men” to “fifty men” and wiped out Song’s entire clan.

sentences.zh: 是時，天下多盜，逢吉自草詔書下州縣，凡盜所居本家及鄰保皆族誅。

translations.literal: At that time bandits were many throughout the realm. Fengji personally drafted edicts sent down to prefectures and counties: wherever a thief dwelled, his original household and the neighboring mutual-responsibility units were all to be exterminated by clan punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits roamed the realm. Fengji drafted edicts to every prefecture and county: wherever a thief lived, his household and his neighbors in mutual-responsibility groups were to be exterminated to the last.

sentences.zh: 或謂逢吉曰：「為盜族誅，已非王法，況鄰保乎！

translations.literal: Someone said to Fengji: “To exterminate clans for theft is already not royal law—how much less the neighboring units!
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Fengji: “Clan slaughter for theft is already beyond the law—how much less for neighbors!

sentences.zh: 」逢吉甗以為是，不得已，但去族誅而已。

translations.literal: ” Fengji rather thought this correct; reluctantly he removed only the clan extermination.
translations.idiomatic: ” Fengji saw the point and, grudgingly, dropped only the clan extermination.

sentences.zh: 於是鄆州捕賊使者張令柔盡殺平陰縣十七村民數百人。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhang Lingrou, the Yanzhou bandit-capture envoy, killed altogether several hundred villagers of seventeen villages in Pingyin County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lingrou, Yanzhou’s bandit-hunter, then slaughtered several hundred people across seventeen villages in Pingyin County.

sentences.zh: 衛州刺史葉仁魯聞部有盜，自帥兵捕之。

translations.literal: The Weizhou prefect Ye Renlu heard there were bandits in his jurisdiction and personally led troops to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou prefect Ye Renlu heard of bandits in his circuit and led troops himself to catch them.

sentences.zh: 時村民十數共逐盜，入於山中，盜皆散走。

translations.literal: At the time more than ten villagers together pursued the bandits into the mountains; the bandits all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: A dozen villagers had chased the bandits into the hills; the bandits had already scattered.

sentences.zh: 仁魯從後至，見民捕盜者，以為賊，悉擒之，斷其腳筋，暴之山麓，宛轉號呼，累日而死。

translations.literal: Renlu arrived from behind, saw the villagers who had chased the bandits, took them for thieves, seized them all, severed their heel tendons, exposed them on the mountain slope—they writhed and wailed for days before dying.
translations.idiomatic: Renlu came up from behind, saw the villagers who had chased the thieves, took them for the gang, seized them all, cut their heel tendons, and left them on the hillside to writhe and scream for days until they died.

sentences.zh: 聞者不勝其冤，而逢吉以仁魯為能，由是天下因盜殺人滋濫。

translations.literal: Those who heard could not bear the injustice; yet Fengji considered Renlu capable—whereby killings on account of banditry grew ever more wanton throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The story sickened listeners—but Fengji praised Renlu’s “efficiency,” and killings in the name of banditry spread without check.

sentences.zh: 逢吉已貴，益為豪侈，謂中書堂食為不可食，乃命家廚進羞，日極珍善。

translations.literal: Once Fengji had grown noble in rank, he became more arrogant and extravagant. He said the Secretariat hall meals were inedible and ordered his household kitchen to bring delicacies—daily feasts of the utmost fineness.
translations.idiomatic: Raised high, Fengji turned ever more lavish. He called the Secretariat’s hall food unfit to eat and had his own kitchen send delicacies—each day a banquet of the rarest fare.

sentences.zh: 繼母死，不服喪。

translations.literal: When his stepmother died, he wore no mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his stepmother died, he wore no mourning garb.

sentences.zh: 妻武氏卒，諷百官及州鎮皆輸綾絹為喪服。

translations.literal: When his wife Lady Wu died, he prompted all officials and prefectures and military commissions to contribute silk for mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Wu died, he pressed every official and every prefecture and command to send silk for mourning robes.

sentences.zh: 武氏未期，除其諸子為官。

translations.literal: Before Lady Wu’s mourning period had passed, he appointed his sons to office.
translations.idiomatic: Before Lady Wu’s mourning year was out, he had his sons appointed to office.

sentences.zh: 有庶兄自外來，未白逢吉而見其諸子，逢吉怒，托以佗事告於高祖，杖殺之。

translations.literal: A half-brother came from outside; without informing Fengji he visited Fengji’s sons. Fengji was furious, found a pretext to report him to the High Ancestor, and had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: A half-brother arrived from abroad and, without telling Fengji, visited his sons. Fengji, enraged, denounced him to the High Ancestor on some other charge and had him clubbed to death.

sentences.zh: 逢吉嘗從高祖征鄴，數使酒辱周太祖於軍中，太祖恨之。

translations.literal: Fengji once followed the High Ancestor on campaign against Ye and repeatedly drunkenly insulted Zhou Taizu in the army—Taizu resented him.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against Ye with the High Ancestor, Fengji repeatedly humiliated Zhou Taizu while drunk—and Taizu never forgot it.

sentences.zh: 其後隱帝立，逢吉素善李濤，諷濤請罷太祖與楊邠樞密。

translations.literal: Afterward the Deposed Emperor ascended. Fengji had long been friendly with Li Tao and prompted Tao to ask that Taizu and Yang Bin be removed from the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, Fengji, who was close to Li Tao, urged Tao to petition for Taizu’s and Yang Bin’s removal from the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 李太后怒濤離間大臣，罷濤相，以楊邠兼平章事，事悉關決。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Li was angry that Tao had sown discord among ministers; she dismissed Tao from the chancellorship and had Yang Bin additionally serve as co-signer—all affairs passed through his decision.
translations.idiomatic: Dowager Li, furious that Tao had set ministers against one another, stripped Tao of the chancellorship and made Yang Bin co-signer as well—every matter now ran through Bin.

sentences.zh: 逢吉、禹珪由是備位而已。

translations.literal: Fengji and Yugui thus filled posts only in name.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji and Yugui were left with titles and nothing else.

sentences.zh: 乾祐二年，加拜司空。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyou he was additionally appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyou year two brought him the Grand Marshal’s seal.

sentences.zh: 周太祖鎮鄴，不落樞密使，逢吉以謂樞密之任，方鎮帶之非便，與史弘肇爭，於是卒如弘肇議。

translations.literal: Zhou Taizu governed Ye but did not relinquish the Privy Council post. Fengji held that for a military commissioner to carry that office was unsuitable and contended with Shi Hongzhao—in the end it went as Hongzhao wished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Taizu held Ye and kept the Privy Council. Fengji argued a frontier governor should not carry that post and fought Shi Hongzhao over it—in the end Hongzhao won.

sentences.zh: 弘肇怨逢吉異己，已而會飲王章第，使酒坐中，弘肇怒甚。

translations.literal: Hongzhao resented Fengji for opposing him. Later they met for drink at Wang Zhang’s residence; Hongzhao drank heavily at table and was very angry.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao resented Fengji’s opposition. At a drinking party at Wang Zhang’s house he drank hard and burned with anger.

sentences.zh: 逢吉謀求出鎮以避之，既而中輟，人問其故，逢吉曰：「茍舍此而去，史公一處分，吾齏粉矣！」

translations.literal: Fengji planned to seek a posting outside the capital to avoid him; then he stopped halfway. When asked why, Fengji said: “If I should leave this post, one order from Lord Shi and I am powder!”
translations.idiomatic: Fengji planned to take a provincial post and escape him—then changed his mind. Asked why, he said: “If I leave this seat, one word from Lord Shi and I am dust!”

sentences.zh: 是時，隱帝少年，小人在側。

translations.literal: At that time the Deposed Emperor was young; petty men were at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor was still a youth; petty men crowded his side.

sentences.zh: 弘肇等威制人主，帝與左右李業、郭允明等皆患之。

translations.literal: Hongzhao and the others overawed and controlled the sovereign; the emperor and those around him—Li Ye, Guo Yunming, and the rest—all chafed at it.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao and his faction overawed the throne; the emperor and his intimates—Li Ye, Guo Yunming, and the rest—all hated it.

sentences.zh: 逢吉每見業等，以言激之，業等卒殺弘肇，即以逢吉權知樞密院。

translations.literal: Whenever Fengji saw Ye and the others he goaded them with words; Ye and the others at last killed Hongzhao and immediately had Fengji serve as acting chief of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji goaded Ye and his circle whenever he saw them; they at last killed Hongzhao and made Fengji acting head of the Privy Council on the spot.

sentences.zh: 方命草麻，聞周太祖起兵，乃止。

translations.literal: Just as he was ordered to draft the edict of appointment, they heard Zhou Taizu had raised troops—and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He was just drafting the appointment edict when word came that Zhou Taizu had risen in arms—and everything halted.

sentences.zh: 逢吉夜宿金祥殿東閣，謂司天夏官正王處訥曰：「昨夕未暝，已見李崧在側，生人接死者，無吉事也。

translations.literal: Fengji lodged by night in the eastern wing of the Jinxian Hall and said to Wang Chune, Director of the Directorate of Astronomy’s Summer Office: “Last night before dark I already saw Li Song at my side—the living meeting the dead: nothing auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji spent the night in the eastern wing of the Jinxian Hall and told Wang Chune, the Summer Office director of astronomy: “Last night, before dusk, I saw Li Song beside me—the living keeping company with the dead. Nothing good can come of that.

sentences.zh: 」周太祖至北郊，官軍敗於劉子陂。

translations.literal: ” Zhou Taizu reached the northern suburbs; the government army was defeated at Liuzi Slope.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhou Taizu reached the northern suburbs; the imperial army broke at Liuzi Slope.

sentences.zh: 逢吉宿七里，夜與同舍酣飲，索刀將自殺，為左右所止。

translations.literal: Fengji lodged at Qili. At night he drank heavily with his lodge-mates, took a knife intending suicide, and was stopped by attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji stopped at Qili. That night he drank deep with his companions, drew a knife to kill himself, and was restrained.

sentences.zh: 明日與隱帝走趙村，自殺於民舍。

translations.literal: The next day he fled with the Deposed Emperor to Zhao Village and killed himself in a commoner’s dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he fled with the Deposed Emperor to Zhao Village and took his life in a private house.

sentences.zh: 周太祖定京師，梟其首，適當李崧被刑之所。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu secured the capital, Fengji’s head was displayed on a pole—just where Li Song had been executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu took the capital, Fengji’s head was hung on a pole—exactly where Li Song had died.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，賜其子西京莊並宅一區。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun, his son was granted an estate in the Western Capital and one mansion precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangshun his son received a Western Capital estate and a mansion.

sentences.zh: 史弘肇

translations.literal: Shi Hongzhao
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao

sentences.zh: 史弘肇，字化元，鄭州滎澤人也。

translations.literal: Shi Hongzhao, styled Huayuan, was a native of Xingze in Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao, styled Huayuan, came from Xingze in Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 為人驍勇，走及奔馬。

translations.literal: As a man he was fierce and brave—he could run and keep pace with a galloping horse.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce and bold—on foot he could keep up with a galloping horse.

sentences.zh: 梁末，調民七戶出一兵，弘肇為兵，隸開道指揮，選為禁兵。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang, seven households were levied for one soldier; Hongzhao became a soldier, attached to the Kaifeng circuit commander, and was selected for the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang’s last days seven households furnished one soldier. Hongzhao served under the Kaifeng circuit commander and was chosen for the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖典禁兵，弘肇為軍校。

translations.literal: When the Han High Ancestor commanded the palace guard, Hongzhao was a company officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han High Ancestor took command of the guard, Hongzhao was a company officer.

sentences.zh: 其後，漢高祖鎮太原，使將武節左右指揮，領雷州刺史。

translations.literal: Afterward the Han High Ancestor governed Taiyuan and had him command the Left and Right Commands of Military Discipline, holding also the prefect of Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later the High Ancestor held Taiyuan and put Hongzhao over the Left and Right Commands of Military Discipline, with Leizhou as his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 高祖建號於太原，代州王暉拒命，弘肇攻破之，以功拜忠武軍節度使、侍衛步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor established his title at Taiyuan, Wang Hui of Daizhou refused orders; Hongzhao broke him and was made Military Governor of Zhongwu and Commander of the Palace Guard Foot Corps for merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor declared his title at Taiyuan, Wang Hui of Daizhou defied him. Hongzhao broke the city and was made Military Governor of Zhongwu and commander of the palace guard foot corps.

sentences.zh: 是時契丹北歸，留耿崇美攻王守恩於潞州。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan were returning north and left Geng Chongmei to attack Wang Shou’en at Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were marching north and left Geng Chongmei to besiege Wang Shou’en at Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣弘肇前行擊之，崇美敗走，守恩以城歸漢。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor sent Hongzhao ahead to strike them; Chongmei was defeated and fled; Shou’en surrendered the city to Han.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor sent Hongzhao forward; Chongmei broke and fled, and Shou’en surrendered Luzhou to Han.

sentences.zh: 而河陽武行德、澤州翟令奇等，皆迎弘肇自歸。

translations.literal: And Wu Xingde of Heyang, Zhai Lingqi of Zezhou, and others all welcomed Hongzhao and submitted on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xingde of Heyang, Zhai Lingqi of Zezhou, and others all came over to Hongzhao of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 弘肇入河陽，高祖從後至，遂入京師。

translations.literal: Hongzhao entered Heyang; the High Ancestor followed from behind and then entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao entered Heyang; the High Ancestor came up behind and then entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 弘肇為將，嚴毅寡言，麾下嘗少忤意，立楇殺之，軍中為股慄，以故高祖起義之初，弘肇行兵所至，秋亳無犯，兩京帖然。

translations.literal: Hongzhao as a general was stern, resolute, and sparing of speech. Under his command, if anyone slightly displeased him he would instantly kill with a club—the army trembled in its thighs. For this reason, at the beginning of the High Ancestor’s uprising, wherever Hongzhao’s troops marched not a hair was harmed and both capitals were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao commanded with iron silence. The least offense and he killed on the spot with a club—the troops shook in their boots. At the start of the High Ancestor’s rising, wherever Hongzhao marched not a blade of grass was touched, and both capitals lay quiet.

sentences.zh: 遷侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使，領歸德軍節度使、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commander of the Palace Guard Cavalry and Foot Corps, holding also Military Governor of Guide and Co-signer of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to commander of the palace guard horse and foot, Military Governor of Guide, and Co-signer of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 高祖疾大漸，與楊邠、蘇逢吉等同授顧命。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor’s illness grew grave, he along with Yang Bin and Su Fengji were together entrusted with the deathbed charge.
translations.idiomatic: As the High Ancestor lay dying, Hongzhao, Yang Bin, and Su Fengji were named together in his final charge.

sentences.zh: 隱帝時，河中李守貞、鳳翔王景崇、永興趙思綰等皆反，關西用兵，人情恐懼，京師之民，流言以相驚恐。

translations.literal: In the Deposed Emperor’s time Li Shouzhen of Hezhong, Wang Jingchong of Fengxiang, Zhao Sixian of Yongxing, and others all rebelled. War was waged in the western passes; hearts were fearful. The people of the capital, by rumor, alarmed one another.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor, Li Shouzhen of Hezhong, Wang Jingchong of Fengxiang, Zhao Sixian of Yongxing, and others rebelled. War opened in the western passes; fear ran through the realm. In the capital rumor fed rumor.

sentences.zh: 弘肇出兵警察，務行殺戮，罪無大小皆死。

translations.literal: Hongzhao went out with troops to police; he insisted on killing—guilt great or small, all died.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao patrolled with troops and killed without distinction—petty crime or great, all went to the block.

sentences.zh: 是時太白晝見，民有仰觀者，輒腰斬於市。

translations.literal: At that time Venus appeared in daytime. Any commoner who looked up to observe it was immediately cut in two at the waist in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Venus showed by day. Any commoner who looked up to watch it was cut in half in the market.

sentences.zh: 市有醉者忤一軍卒，誣其訛言，坐棄市。

translations.literal: In the market a drunk crossed a soldier; the soldier falsely accused him of spreading false rumors—he was executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: A drunk in the market crossed a soldier; the soldier accused him of spreading sedition—and he was executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 凡民抵罪，吏以白弘肇，但以三指示之，吏即腰斬之。

translations.literal: Whenever a commoner was charged, the clerk reported to Hongzhao; Hongzhao need only point with three fingers and the clerk would cut the man in two at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: When a commoner was charged, the clerk told Hongzhao; three fingers from Hongzhao and the clerk cut the man in half.

sentences.zh: 又為斷舌、決口、斮筋、折足之刑。

translations.literal: He also imposed punishments of severing the tongue, splitting the mouth, cutting tendons, and breaking feet.
translations.idiomatic: He added punishments of severed tongues, split mouths, cut sinews, and broken feet.

sentences.zh: 李崧坐奴告變族誅，弘肇取其幼女以為婢。

translations.literal: Li Song was exterminated by clan punishment after a slave reported treason; Hongzhao took his young daughter as a maidservant.
translations.idiomatic: Li Song’s clan was wiped out after a slave denounced him; Hongzhao took his young daughter for a maid.

sentences.zh: 於是前資故將失職之家，姑息僮奴，而廝養之輩，往往脅制其主。

translations.literal: Thereupon in households of former officials, old generals fallen from office, they indulged their page-boys and slaves—and the menials often coerced their masters.
translations.idiomatic: Former officials and dismissed generals indulged their pages and slaves—and the servants often ruled the house.

sentences.zh: 侍衛孔目官解暉狡酷，因緣為奸，民抵罪者，莫敢告訴。

translations.literal: The palace guard clerical officer Xie Hui was cunning and cruel and used opportunity to do wrong; commoners who were charged dared not appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui, a palace guard clerk, was sly and savage; anyone he charged dared not complain.

sentences.zh: 燕人何福進有玉枕，直錢十四萬，遣僮賣之淮南以鬻茶。

translations.literal: He Yan Fujin of Yan had a jade pillow worth 140,000 cash; he sent a page to sell it in Huainan to trade for tea.
translations.idiomatic: He Fujin of Yan owned a jade pillow worth 140,000 cash and sent a page to sell it in Huainan for tea.

sentences.zh: 僮隱其錢，福進笞責之，僮乃誣告福進得趙延壽玉枕，以遺吳人。

translations.literal: The page hid the money; Fujin whipped and rebuked him. The page then falsely reported that Fujin had obtained Zhao Yanshou’s jade pillow and was giving it to men of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The page kept the money; Fujin beat him. The page then lied that Fujin had Zhao Yanshou’s jade pillow and meant to send it to Wu.

sentences.zh: 弘肇捕治，福進棄市，帳下分取其妻子，而籍其家財。

translations.literal: Hongzhao arrested and tried him; Fujin was executed in the market. Hongzhao’s staff divided his wife and children among themselves and registered his household wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao seized him; Fujin was executed in the market. Hongzhao’s men divided his wife and children among themselves and seized his property.

sentences.zh: 弘肇不喜賓客，嘗言：「文人難耐，呼我為卒。」

translations.literal: Hongzhao did not like guests. He once said: “Literati are unbearable—they call me a soldier.”
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao disliked company. He once said: “Scholars are insufferable—they call me a common soldier.”

sentences.zh: 弘肇領歸德，其副使等月率私錢千緡為獻。

translations.literal: Hongzhao held Guide; his deputies and the like monthly offered a thousand strings of private cash as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Guide, his deputies each month sent him a thousand strings of private cash.

sentences.zh: 潁州麹場官麹溫與軍將何拯爭官務，訟之三司，三司直溫。

translations.literal: The Yongzhou yeast-works officer Qu Wen and the army officer He Zheng disputed official business and sued at the Three Departments; the Three Departments ruled for Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Wen of the Yongzhou yeast office and the officer He Zheng quarreled over duty and sued before the Three Departments, which ruled for Wen.

sentences.zh: 拯訴之弘肇，弘肇以謂潁己屬州，而溫不先白己，乃追溫殺之，連坐者數十人。

translations.literal: Zheng appealed to Hongzhao. Hongzhao held that Ying was already his subordinate prefecture and Wen had not first informed him—he had Wen pursued and killed; dozens were implicated and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng appealed to Hongzhao. Hongzhao said Ying was his circuit and Wen had not cleared matters with him first—he had Wen hunted down and killed, and dozens were punished with him.

sentences.zh: 周太祖平李守貞，推功群臣，弘肇拜中書令。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu pacified Li Shouzhen he spread credit among the ministers; Hongzhao was appointed Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu crushed Li Shouzhen he shared credit among the ministers; Hongzhao was made Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 隱帝自關西罷兵，漸近小人，與後贊、李業等嬉遊無度，而太后親族頗行幹托，弘肇與楊邠稍裁抑之。

translations.literal: After the Deposed Emperor ended warfare in the western passes he drew gradually near petty men, sporting without measure with Hou Zan, Li Ye, and the rest; meanwhile the empress dowager’s kin often practiced influence-peddling. Hongzhao and Yang Bin somewhat checked and restrained this.
translations.idiomatic: When the western war ended the Deposed Emperor drifted toward petty favorites—Hou Zan, Li Ye, and the rest—and played without restraint. The dowager’s kin peddled influence; Hongzhao and Yang Bin checked them where they could.

sentences.zh: 太后有故人子求補軍職，弘肇輒斬之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager had an old acquaintance’s son who sought to be appointed to a military post—Hongzhao instantly had him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager’s old friend’s son sought a military post—Hongzhao had him beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 帝始聽樂，賜教坊使等玉帶、錦袍，往謝弘肇，弘肇怒曰：「健兒為國征行者未有偏賜，爾曹何功，敢當此乎！

translations.literal: The emperor first listened to music and gave the directors of the Music Bureau jade belts and brocade robes. They went to thank Hongzhao. Hongzhao angrily said: “Stalwart soldiers campaigning for the state have received no special gifts—what merit have you people that you dare accept this!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first heard music and gave the Music Bureau directors jade belts and brocade robes. They came to thank Hongzhao. He raged: “Hard soldiers on campaign get no such gifts—what have you done to deserve this!

sentences.zh: 」悉取所賜還官。

translations.literal: ” He took back everything they had been given and returned it to the government.
translations.idiomatic: ” He stripped them of every gift and sent it all back to the treasury.

sentences.zh: 周太祖出鎮魏州，弘肇議帶樞密行，蘇逢吉、楊邠以為不可，弘肇恨之。

translations.literal: Zhou Taizu went out to govern Weizhou. Hongzhao proposed carrying the Privy Council post with him; Su Fengji and Yang Bin thought it impossible—Hongzhao resented them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Taizu went out to govern Weizhou. Hongzhao wanted to keep the Privy Council and go; Su Fengji and Yang Bin refused—and Hongzhao hated them for it.

sentences.zh: 明日，會飲竇貞固第，弘肇厲聲舉爵屬太祖曰：「昨日廷論，何為異同？

translations.literal: The next day they met for drink at Dou Zhengu’s residence. Hongzhao raised his cup in a loud voice and directed it at Taizu, saying: “Yesterday at court we argued—why the disagreement?
translations.idiomatic: Next day they drank at Dou Zhengu’s house. Hongzhao lifted his cup toward Taizu and said in a hard voice: “Yesterday in court we split—why?

sentences.zh: 今日與公飲此。

translations.literal: Today I drink this with you, sir.
translations.idiomatic: Today I drink with you, sir.

sentences.zh: 」逢吉與邠亦舉大爵曰：「此國家事也，何必介意乎！

translations.literal: ” Fengji and Bin also raised great cups and said: “This is state business—why take it to heart!
translations.idiomatic: ” Fengji and Bin raised their cups too: “This is the realm’s business—why hold a grudge!

sentences.zh: 」遂俱飲釂。

translations.literal: ” They then all drained their cups.
translations.idiomatic: ” They drained their cups together.

sentences.zh: 弘肇曰：「安朝廷，定禍亂，直須長槍大劍，若『毛錐子』安足用哉？

translations.literal: Hongzhao said: “To secure the court and still chaos, one needs long spears and great swords—what use are ‘hair awls’?
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao said: “To settle the court and stop calamity you need long spears and great swords—what good are ‘hair awls’?

sentences.zh: 」三司使王章曰：「無『毛錐子』，軍賦何從集乎？

translations.literal: Three Departments commissioner Wang Zhang said: “Without ‘hair awls,’ whence come military taxes?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang, commissioner of the Three Departments, said: “Without ‘hair awls,’ where do military taxes come from?

sentences.zh: 」「毛錐子」，蓋言筆也。

translations.literal: ” “Hair awls”—that is to say, writing brushes.
translations.idiomatic: ” “Hair awls” meant writing brushes.

sentences.zh: 弘肇默然。

translations.literal: Hongzhao fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao said nothing.

sentences.zh: 他日，會飲章第，酒酣，為手勢令，弘肇不能為，客省使閻晉卿坐次弘肇，屢教之。

translations.literal: Another day they met for drink at Zhang’s residence. When the wine was deep they played hand-gesture forfeits; Hongzhao could not do it. The Guest Liaison Commissioner Yan Jinqing sat below Hongzhao and repeatedly taught him.
translations.idiomatic: Another day they drank at Zhang’s house. Wine deep, they played hand-gesture forfeits; Hongzhao could not manage. Yan Jinqing of the Guest Liaison Office sat below him and kept showing him how.

sentences.zh: 蘇逢吉戲曰：「坐有姓閻人，何憂罰爵！

translations.literal: Su Fengji jestingly said: “With someone surnamed Yan at the table, why worry about penalty cups!
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji joked: “With a Yan at the table, who fears a penalty cup!

sentences.zh: 」弘肇妻閻氏，酒家倡，以為譏己，大怒，以醜語詬逢吉，逢吉不校。

translations.literal: ” Hongzhao’s wife was Lady Yan—a wine-shop singer—and she thought herself mocked. Greatly angered, she reviled Fengji with ugly words; Fengji did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: ” Hongzhao’s wife was Lady Yan, once a wine-shop singer; she took it as a jibe at her. She flew into a rage and cursed Fengji with foul words. Fengji did not reply.

sentences.zh: 弘肇欲毆之，逢吉先出。

translations.literal: Hongzhao wanted to beat him; Fengji left first.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao meant to strike him; Fengji slipped out first.

sentences.zh: 弘肇起索劍欲追之，楊邠泣曰：「蘇公，漢宰相，公若殺之，致天子何地乎？

translations.literal: Hongzhao rose to seek a sword and chase him. Yang Bin wept and said: “Lord Su is Han’s chancellor. If you kill him, where will you leave the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao rose for his sword to run him down. Yang Bin wept: “Su is Han’s chancellor. Kill him—and where does that leave the emperor?

sentences.zh: 」弘肇馳馬去，邠送至第而還。

translations.literal: ” Hongzhao rode off; Bin escorted him to his residence and returned.
translations.idiomatic: ” Hongzhao galloped away. Bin saw Fengji home and came back.

sentences.zh: 由是將相如水火。

translations.literal: From this the ministers were like fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: After that the ministers were fire and water.

sentences.zh: 隱帝遣王峻置酒公子亭和解之。

translations.literal: The Hidden Emperor sent Wang Jun to set wine at the Prince’s Pavilion and reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Emperor sent Wang Jun to pour wine at the Prince’s Pavilion and force a truce.

sentences.zh: 是時，李業、郭允明、後贊、聶文進等用事，不喜執政。

translations.literal: At that time Li Ye, Guo Yunming, Hou Zan, Nie Wenjin, and others held sway and disliked the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye, Guo Yunming, Hou Zan, Nie Wenjin, and others held the court and hated the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 而隱帝春秋漸長，為大臣所制，數有忿言，業等乘間譖之，以謂弘肇威震人主，不除必為亂。

translations.literal: The Hidden Emperor was gradually growing older and felt hemmed in by the great ministers; he often spoke in anger. Ye and the rest seized the moment to slander them, saying Hongzhao’s power overawed the ruler and that if he were not removed he would surely bring rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was coming of age and chafed under his ministers; he muttered his anger. Ye and his circle whispered that Hongzhao overawed the throne and would bring rebellion if left alive.

sentences.zh: 隱帝頗欲除之。

translations.literal: The Hidden Emperor very much wished to remove them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted them gone.

sentences.zh: 夜聞作坊鍛甲聲，以為兵至，達旦不寐。

translations.literal: At night he heard the sound of armor being forged in the workshops and thought troops had come; until dawn he could not sleep.
translations.idiomatic: One night he heard armor being hammered in the workshops and thought the army was upon him. He lay awake until dawn.

sentences.zh: 由是與業等密謀禁中。

translations.literal: From this he secretly plotted with Ye and the rest within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He began to plot with Ye and the rest behind palace walls.

sentences.zh: 乾祐三年冬十月十三日，弘肇與楊邠、王章等入朝，坐廣政殿東廡，甲士數十人自內出，擒弘肇、邠、章斬之，並族其三家。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the tenth month, winter, in the third year of Qianyou, Hongzhao entered court with Yang Bin and Wang Zhang and the rest. They sat in the eastern gallery of Guangzheng Hall. Several dozen armored soldiers came out from within, seized Hongzhao, Bin, and Zhang, and beheaded them—and exterminated all three clans.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth of the tenth month, Qianyou year three, Hongzhao came to court with Yang Bin and Wang Zhang and sat in the eastern gallery of Guangzheng Hall. Dozens of armored men burst from within, seized the three, and beheaded them—and wiped out every clan.

sentences.zh: 楊邠，魏州冠氏人也。

translations.literal: Yang Bin was a native of Guanshi in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bin came from Guanshi in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 少為州掌籍吏，租庸使孔謙領度支，補邠勾押官，歷孟、華、鄆三州糧料院使。

translations.literal: In youth he was a clerk keeping registers for the prefecture. Kong Qian of the Tax and Corvée Bureau oversaw revenue and appointed Bin auditing officer; he served successively as grain commissioner for Meng, Hua, and Yun prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he kept the prefectural registers. Kong Qian of the Tax and Corvée Bureau made him auditing officer; he rose through grain commissions in Meng, Hua, and Yun.

sentences.zh: 事漢高祖為右都押衙，高祖即位，拜樞密使。

translations.literal: Serving Han’s High Ancestor as right chief adjutant, when the High Ancestor took the throne he was made Privy Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han’s High Ancestor he was right chief adjutant; at enthronement he became Privy Councilor.

sentences.zh: 邠出於小吏，不喜文士，與蘇逢吉等內相排忌。

translations.literal: Bin came from petty clerks and disliked men of letters; within the court he and Su Fengji and others mutually excluded and resented one another.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk by origin, he despised scholars; he and Su Fengji and their factions feuded in court.

sentences.zh: 逢吉諷李濤上疏罷邠與周太祖樞密使，邠泣訴李太后前，太后怒，罷濤相，加邠中書侍郎兼吏部尚書、同平章事。

translations.literal: Fengji prompted Li Tao to memorial asking that Bin and Zhou Taizu be removed from the Privy Council. Bin wept and pleaded before Empress Dowager Li; the dowager was furious, dismissed Tao from the chancellorship, and made Bin Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Minister of Personnel, and Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji urged Li Tao to petition for Bin’s and Guo Wei’s removal from the Privy Council. Bin wept before Dowager Li; she raged, ousted Tao, and made Bin Vice Director, Minister of Personnel, and Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 是時，逢吉、禹珪頗以私賄除吏，多繆。

translations.literal: At that time Fengji and Yu Gui often appointed officials through private bribes, and many appointments were wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji and Yu Gui sold offices for bribes; appointments went wildly astray.

sentences.zh: 邠為相，事無大小，必先示邠，邠以為可，乃入白，而深革逢吉所為，凡門蔭出身，諸司補吏者，一切罷之。

translations.literal: When Bin became chancellor, matters great and small were first shown to Bin; if Bin thought them acceptable, only then were they reported upward—and he deeply overturned what Fengji had done. Every appointment by hereditary privilege or bureau supplement was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor, nothing passed until Bin approved—and he tore up Fengji’s work. Hereditary appointments and bureau supplements were all cancelled.

sentences.zh: 邠雖長於吏事，而不知大體，以謂為國家者，帑廩實、甲兵完而已，禮樂文物皆虛器也。

translations.literal: Though Bin was skilled in clerical affairs, he did not grasp the larger pattern. He held that to govern a state one need only fill the treasury and complete the armor; rites, music, and cultural institutions were empty vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Bin knew ledgers, not statecraft. A full treasury and sharp swords—that, he said, was government; rites, music, and culture were empty show.

sentences.zh: 以故秉大政而務苛細，凡前資官不得居外，而天下行旅，皆給過所然後得行。

translations.literal: Therefore, holding great power, he pursued petty strictness. Former officials could not serve outside the capital; travelers everywhere had to be given travel passes before they might go.
translations.idiomatic: In power he ruled by petty strictness. Former officials could not leave the capital; every traveler needed a pass.

sentences.zh: 旬日之間，人情大擾，邠度不可行而止。

translations.literal: Within ten days popular feeling was greatly disturbed; Bin judged it could not be done and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the realm seethed; Bin saw it would not hold and backed off.

sentences.zh: 邠常與王章論事帝前，帝曰：「事行之後，勿使有言也！

translations.literal: Bin often discussed affairs with Wang Zhang before the emperor. The emperor said: “After a matter is done, let there be no talk of it!
translations.idiomatic: Bin often debated policy with Wang Zhang before the throne. The emperor said: “Once a thing is done, let no one speak of it!

sentences.zh: 」邠遽曰：「陛下但禁聲，有臣在。

translations.literal: ” Bin blurted: “Your Majesty need only forbid talk—I am here.
translations.idiomatic: ” Bin snapped: “Your Majesty need only silence tongues. I am here.

sentences.zh: 」聞者為之戰慄。

translations.literal: ” Those who heard trembled.
translations.idiomatic: ” Men who heard it shook.

sentences.zh: 李太后弟業求為宣徽使，帝與太后私以問邠，邠止以為不可。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Li’s younger brother Ye sought to be Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat. The emperor and the dowager privately asked Bin; Bin would only say it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager’s brother Ye wanted the Palace Secretariat commission. Emperor and dowager asked Bin in private; he said no.

sentences.zh: 帝欲立所愛耿夫人為後，邠又以為不可；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make his beloved Lady Geng empress; Bin again thought it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to make his beloved Lady Geng empress; Bin again refused.

sentences.zh: 夫人死，將以後禮葬之，邠又以為不可。

translations.literal: When the lady died and he meant to bury her with empress rites, Bin again thought it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When she died and he meant to bury her as empress, Bin refused once more.

sentences.zh: 由是隱帝大怒，而左右乘間構之，與史弘肇等同日見殺。

translations.literal: From this the Hidden Emperor was greatly enraged, and those around him seized the moment to set him against Bin; on the same day as Shi Hongzhao he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor boiled with rage; courtiers drove the wedge deeper. He died the same day as Shi Hongzhao.

sentences.zh: 邠為人頗儉靜，四方之賂雖不卻，然往往以獻於帝。

translations.literal: Bin was by nature rather frugal and quiet. Though he did not refuse bribes from the four directions, he often presented them to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Bin lived frugally and quietly. He took bribes from every quarter—but often turned them over to the throne.

sentences.zh: 居家謝絕賓客，晚節稍通縉紳，延客門下。

translations.literal: At home he shut out guests; in his later years he opened somewhat to gentry and kept guests at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: At home he turned guests away; late in life he opened his gate a little to the gentry.

sentences.zh: 知史傳有用，乃課吏傳寫。

translations.literal: Knowing history had use, he set clerks to copy it.
translations.idiomatic: He thought history worth keeping and set clerks to copying it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，及於禍。

translations.literal: Before long he met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, disaster found him.

sentences.zh: 周太祖即位，追封弘農王。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu took the throne, Bin was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Taizu posthumously made him Prince of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 王章，魏州南樂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhang was a native of Nanle in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang came from Nanle in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 為州孔目官，張令昭逐節度使劉延皓，章事令昭。

translations.literal: He was a prefectural clerk. When Zhang Lingzhao drove out military commissioner Liu Yanhao, Zhang served Lingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was a prefectural clerk. When Zhang Lingzhao ousted Liu Yanhao, Zhang served him.

sentences.zh: 令昭敗，章婦翁白文珂與副招討李周善，乃以章托周。

translations.literal: When Lingzhao was defeated, Zhang’s father-in-law Bai Wenke was on good terms with Deputy Pacification Commissioner Li Zhou; he entrusted Zhang to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhao fell; Zhang’s father-in-law Bai Wenke knew Deputy Pacification Commissioner Li Zhou and put Zhang in Zhou’s hands.

sentences.zh: 周匿章褚中，以橐駝負之洛陽，藏周第。

translations.literal: Zhou hid Zhang in a leather bag and had a camel carry him to Luoyang, concealing him in Zhou’s residence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou hid him in a leather sack, had a camel carry him to Luoyang, and kept him in his house.

sentences.zh: 唐滅，章乃出，為河陽糧料使。

translations.literal: When Tang fell, Zhang came out and became grain commissioner of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang fell he emerged and became Heyang grain commissioner.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖典禁兵，補章孔目官，從之太原。

translations.literal: When Han’s High Ancestor commanded the palace guard, Zhang was made clerk and followed him to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Han’s High Ancestor took the palace guard, Zhang became his clerk and followed him to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，拜三司使、檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor took the throne, Zhang was made commissioner of the Three Departments and Acting Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: At enthronement Zhang became Three Departments commissioner and Acting Grand General.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，隱帝即位，加太尉、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor died and the Hidden Emperor succeeded, Zhang was made Grand General and Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor died; the Hidden Emperor made Zhang Grand General and Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 是時，漢方新造，承契丹之後，京師空乏，而關西三叛作，周太祖用兵西方，章供饋軍旅，未嘗乏絕。

translations.literal: At that time Han was newly founded, coming after the Khitan; the capital was empty and poor. The three western rebellions arose; Zhou Taizu campaigned in the west. Zhang supplied the armies and never fell short.
translations.idiomatic: Han was newborn, the capital drained after the Khitan, and the west in revolt. Guo Wei marched west; Zhang fed the armies without fail.

sentences.zh: 然征利剝下，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: Yet he squeezed profit from the people below, and the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he squeezed the people, and they suffered.

sentences.zh: 往時民租一石輸二升為「雀鼠耗」，章乃增一石輸二斗為「省耗」；

translations.literal: Formerly the people’s grain rent had two sheng per shi taken as “sparrow-and-rat wastage”; Zhang increased it to two dou per shi and called it “provincial wastage.”
translations.idiomatic: Once two sheng per shi of rent was lost to “sparrow-and-rat wastage”; Zhang raised it to two dou and called it “provincial wastage.”

sentences.zh: 緡錢出入，皆以八十為陌，章減其出者陌三；

translations.literal: When cash went in and out, eighty counted as one string; Zhang reduced outgoing strings by three.
translations.idiomatic: Cash was counted eighty to the string; Zhang shaved three off every string paid out.

sentences.zh: 州縣民訴田者，必全州縣覆之，以括其隱田。

translations.literal: When people in prefectures and counties sued over fields, the whole prefecture or county was re-surveyed to expose hidden land.
translations.idiomatic: One field dispute and the whole county was resurveyed to flush out hidden acres.

sentences.zh: 天下由此重困。

translations.literal: Under heaven the people were thereby doubly burdened.
translations.idiomatic: The realm groaned under the double weight.

sentences.zh: 然尤不喜文士，嘗語人曰：「此輩與一把算子，未知顛倒，何益於國邪！

translations.literal: Yet he especially disliked men of letters. He once told people: “Give this lot an abacus and they still cannot tell which way is up—what good are they to the state?
translations.idiomatic: He hated scholars above all. He said: “Hand these people an abacus and they cannot tell up from down—what use are they to the state?

sentences.zh: 」百官俸廩，皆取供軍之余不堪者，命有司高估其價，估定又增，謂之「擡估」，章猶意不能滿，往往復增之。

translations.literal: ” The hundred offices’ salaries and grain allotments were all taken from what remained after supplying the army—what was unfit for use. He ordered the offices to appraise it high; after appraisal they raised it again—this was called “inflated appraisal.” Zhang still thought it insufficient and often raised it again.
translations.idiomatic: ” Officials were paid from army leftovers unfit for soldiers. Offices inflated the price, then inflated it again—“inflated appraisal.” Zhang still was not satisfied and raised it yet again.

sentences.zh: 民有犯鹽、礬、酒曲者，無多少皆抵死，吏緣為奸，民莫堪命。

translations.literal: People who violated salt, alum, or yeast laws, in whatever amount, all died for it. Clerks used this to commit fraud; the people could not bear life.
translations.idiomatic: Salt, alum, or yeast—any breach, any amount, meant death. Clerks turned the law to theft; life became unbearable.

sentences.zh: 已而與史弘肇等同日見殺。

translations.literal: Before long he was killed on the same day as Shi Hongzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died the same day as Shi Hongzhao.

sentences.zh: 劉銖，陜州人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhu was a native of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhu came from Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 少為梁邵王牙將，與漢高祖有舊，高祖鎮太原，以為左都押衙。

translations.literal: In youth he was a guard officer to Liang’s Prince of Shao and had old ties with Han’s High Ancestor. When the High Ancestor governed Taiyuan he was made left chief adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Youth found him a guard to Liang’s Prince of Shao; he knew Han’s High Ancestor from old days. At Taiyuan the High Ancestor made him left chief adjutant.

sentences.zh: 銖為人慘酷好殺戮，高祖以為勇斷類己，特信用之。

translations.literal: Zhu was by nature cruel and fond of killing. The High Ancestor thought him bold and resolute like himself and trusted him especially.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was cruel and loved blood. The High Ancestor saw his own ruthlessness in him and trusted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，拜永興軍節度使，徙鎮平盧，加檢校太師、同平章事，又加侍中。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor took the throne, Zhu was made military commissioner of Yongxing, then transferred to govern Pinglu, promoted Acting Grand Preceptor and Associate Grand Councilor, and later made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At enthronement Zhu governed Yongxing, then Pinglu; he rose to Acting Grand Preceptor, Associate Grand Councilor, and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 是時，江淮不通，吳越錢镠使者常泛海以至中國。

translations.literal: At that time the Jiang-Huai route was cut; envoys of Qian Liu of Wu-Yue often crossed the sea to reach China.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang-Huai route was severed; Qian Liu’s envoys crossed the sea to reach the court.

sentences.zh: 而濱海諸州皆置博易務，與民貿易。

translations.literal: Coastal prefectures all set up trade offices and traded with the people.
translations.idiomatic: Every coastal prefecture opened trade offices and bartered with the people.

sentences.zh: 民負失期者，務吏擅自攝治，置刑獄，不關州縣。

translations.literal: When people defaulted on debts past due, office clerks on their own authority seized and punished them, set up prisons, and did not report to prefectures or counties.
translations.idiomatic: Debtors who missed a deadline were seized by trade-office clerks, jailed on their own authority, without prefectural oversight.

sentences.zh: 而前為吏者，納其厚賂，縱之不問。

translations.literal: Former clerks took heavy bribes and let offenders go without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Former clerks took fat bribes and looked the other way.

sentences.zh: 民頗為苦，銖乃一切禁之。

translations.literal: The people suffered for it; Zhu then forbade it entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The people bled for it; Zhu banned the whole trade.

sentences.zh: 然銖用法，亦自為刻深。

translations.literal: Yet Zhu’s use of law was also harsh in his own way.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu’s own justice was no less brutal.

sentences.zh: 民有過者，問其年幾何，對曰若干，即隨其數杖之，謂之「隨年杖」。

translations.literal: When a person had committed an offense, he asked how many years old he was; when the man answered so many, he beat him that many strokes—this was called “strokes-by-age.”
translations.idiomatic: He asked an offender his age—and gave him that many strokes. They called it “strokes-by-age.”

sentences.zh: 每杖一人，必兩杖俱下，謂之「合歡杖」。

translations.literal: Each time he beat one man, both sticks had to fall together—this was called “paired strokes.”
translations.idiomatic: Each beating required both sticks to fall at once—“paired strokes.”

sentences.zh: 又請增民租，畝出錢三十以為公用，民不堪之。

translations.literal: He also asked to increase the people’s rent—thirty cash per mu for public use—and the people could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: He also demanded thirty cash per mu in rent for public use; the people buckled.

sentences.zh: 隱帝患銖剛暴，召之，懼不至。

translations.literal: The Hidden Emperor resented Zhu’s harshness and summoned him; he feared Zhu would not come.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated Zhu’s violence and summoned him, fearing he would not obey.

sentences.zh: 是時，沂州郭淮攻南唐還，以兵駐青州，隱帝乃遣符彥卿往代銖。

translations.literal: At that time Guo Huai of Yizhou, returning from attacking Southern Tang, stationed troops at Qingzhou; the Hidden Emperor sent Fu Yanqing to replace Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai of Yizhou was back from raiding Southern Tang with troops at Qingzhou; the emperor sent Fu Yanqing to replace Zhu.

sentences.zh: 銖顧禁兵在，莫敢有異意，乃受代還京師。

translations.literal: Zhu saw the palace guard present and dared show no dissent; he accepted replacement and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu saw the palace guard and dared not resist; he yielded his command and returned to court.

sentences.zh: 銖嘗切齒於史弘肇、楊邠等，已而弘肇等死，銖謂李業等曰：「諸君可謂僂儸兒矣。

translations.literal: Zhu had often gnashed his teeth at Shi Hongzhao, Yang Bin, and the rest. After Hongzhao and the others died, Zhu told Li Ye and the rest: “You gentlemen may be called spineless wretches.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu had long ground his teeth at Shi Hongzhao and Yang Bin. When they fell, he told Li Ye’s circle: “You lot are spineless wretches.

sentences.zh: 」權知開封府，周太祖兵犯京師，銖悉誅太祖與王峻等家屬。

translations.literal: ” Acting as governor of Kaifeng, when Zhou Taizu’s army threatened the capital Zhu executed the families of Taizu and Wang Jun and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: ” As acting governor of Kaifeng, when Guo Wei’s army closed on the capital Zhu slaughtered Guo Wei’s and Wang Jun’s households.

sentences.zh: 太祖入京師，銖妻裸露以席自蔽，與銖俱見執。

translations.literal: When Taizu entered the capital, Zhu’s wife bared herself and covered herself with a mat; she and Zhu were both seized.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei entered the capital. Zhu’s wife stripped and hid behind a mat; both were taken.

sentences.zh: 銖謂其妻曰：「我則死矣，汝應與人為婢。

translations.literal: Zhu told his wife: “I shall die; you will become someone’s servant girl.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu told his wife: “I die. You will be someone’s servant.

sentences.zh: 」太祖使人責銖曰：「與公共事先帝，獨無故人之情乎？

translations.literal: ” Taizu sent a man to rebuke Zhu: “We served the late emperor together—have you no feeling for an old comrade?
translations.idiomatic: ” Guo Wei sent word: “We served the late emperor together—where is old friendship?

sentences.zh: 吾家屠滅，雖有君命，加之酷毒，一何忍也。

translations.literal: My household was wiped out. Though there was an imperial order, you added cruelty on top—how could you bear it?
translations.idiomatic: My house was wiped out. An imperial order is one thing—your cruelty was another. How could you?

sentences.zh: 今公亦有妻子，獨念之乎？

translations.literal: Now you too have wife and children—do you not think of them?
translations.idiomatic: You have wife and children too—do you think of them?

sentences.zh: 」銖曰：「為漢誅叛臣爾，豈知其佗。

translations.literal: ” Zhu said: “I executed Han’s rebel ministers—that is all. How should I know anything else?
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhu said: “I killed Han’s rebels. Nothing more.

sentences.zh: 」是時，太祖方欲歸人心，乃與群臣議曰：「劉侍中墜馬傷甚，而軍士逼辱，迨有微生，吾欲奏太后，貸其家屬，何如？

translations.literal: ” At that time Taizu wished to win hearts and discussed with his ministers: “Vice Director Liu fell from his horse and was badly hurt; soldiers pressed and humiliated him, yet he barely lives. I wish to memorialize the dowager and spare his household—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: ” Guo Wei meant to win hearts and asked his ministers: “Vice Director Liu fell hard from his horse; soldiers humiliated him, yet he lives. I would ask the dowager to spare his family—what say you?

sentences.zh: 」群臣皆以為善。

translations.literal: ” The ministers all thought it good.
translations.idiomatic: ” The ministers approved.

sentences.zh: 乃止殺銖，與李業等梟首於市，赦其妻子。

translations.literal: He then stayed Zhu’s execution and, with Li Ye and the rest, exposed their heads in the market; their wives and children were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed Zhu’s death. Li Ye and the rest were exposed in the market; their wives and children were spared.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，賜陜州莊宅各一區。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, he granted one estate each in Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At enthronement Guo Wei granted each a Shaanzhou estate.

sentences.zh: 李業，高祖皇后之弟也。

translations.literal: Li Ye was the younger brother of the High Ancestor’s empress.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye was brother to the High Ancestor’s empress.

sentences.zh: 後昆弟七人，業最幼，故尤憐之。

translations.literal: The empress had seven brothers; Ye was the youngest, and therefore especially doted upon.
translations.idiomatic: Seven brothers she had; Ye was youngest and most favored.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，以為武德使。

translations.literal: Under the High Ancestor he was made Commissioner of Martial Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Under the High Ancestor he held the Martial Virtue commission.

sentences.zh: 隱帝即位，業以皇太后故，益用事，無顧憚。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Emperor succeeded, because of the empress dowager Ye wielded power still more and feared nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Emperor’s reign let Ye rule through the dowager, without restraint.

sentences.zh: 時天下旱、蝗，黃河決溢，京師大風拔木，壞城門，宮中數見怪物投瓦石、撼門扉。

translations.literal: At that time drought and locusts afflicted the realm; the Yellow River burst its banks; a great wind in the capital uprooted trees and broke city gates; within the palace monsters were often seen throwing tiles and stones and shaking doors.
translations.idiomatic: Drought and locusts scourged the land; the Yellow River broke; wind uprooted trees and smashed gates; in the palace things threw stones and rattled doors.

sentences.zh: 隱帝召司天趙延乂問禳除之法，延乂對曰：「臣職天象日時，察其變動，以考順逆吉兇而已，禳除之事，非臣所知也。

translations.literal: The Hidden Emperor summoned the Director of Astronomy Zhao Yanyi and asked methods of expiation. Yanyi answered: “My office watches the heavens, day and time, observes their changes, and examines fortune and misfortune, compliance and rebellion—that is all. Matters of expiation are not within my knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called Zhao Yanyi of the Astronomy Bureau and asked how to expiate the omens. Yanyi said: “I read heaven’s changes and judge fortune and ruin—that is my charge. Expiation is not mine to know.

sentences.zh: 然臣所聞，殆山魈也。

translations.literal: Yet what I have heard—it is likely a mountain demon.
translations.idiomatic: What I have heard sounds like a mountain demon.

sentences.zh: 」皇太后乃召尼誦佛書以禳之，一尼如廁，既還，悲泣不知人者數日，及醒訊之，莫知其然。

translations.literal: ” The empress dowager then summoned nuns to chant Buddhist scriptures for expiation. One nun went to the privy; when she returned she wept in grief and did not know herself for several days; when she woke and was questioned, no one knew why.
translations.idiomatic: ” The dowager sent nuns to chant sutras. One went to the privy; she returned weeping, lost to herself for days, and when she woke could explain nothing.

sentences.zh: 而帝方與業及聶文進、後贊、郭允明等狎昵，多為廋語相誚戲，放紙鳶於宮中。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the emperor was on intimate terms with Ye, Nie Wenjin, Hou Zan, Guo Yunming, and the rest, often trading veiled jests and mockery, flying paper kites in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meanwhile caroused with Ye, Nie Wenjin, Hou Zan, and Guo Yunming—veiled jests, mockery, paper kites in the palace.

sentences.zh: 太后數以災異戒帝，不聽。

translations.literal: The empress dowager repeatedly warned the emperor with omens and disasters; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager warned him with every omen; he would not hear.

sentences.zh: 時宣徽使闕，業欲得之，太后亦遣人諷大臣。

translations.literal: At that time the Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat was vacant; Ye wished to obtain it, and the empress dowager also sent men to hint the great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Secretariat commission stood empty; Ye wanted it, and the dowager hinted the ministers.

sentences.zh: 大臣楊邠、史弘肇等皆以為不可。

translations.literal: The great ministers Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and the rest all thought it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and the rest all refused.

sentences.zh: 業由此怨望，謀殺邠等。

translations.literal: From this Ye nursed resentment and plotted to kill Bin and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Ye nursed the grudge and plotted their deaths.

sentences.zh: 邠等已死。

translations.literal: Bin and the rest were already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Bin and the rest were dead.

sentences.zh: 又遣供奉官孟業以詔書殺郭威於魏州。

translations.literal: He again sent Palace Attendant Meng Ye with an edict to kill Guo Wei at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Palace Attendant Meng Ye with an edict to kill Guo Wei at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 威舉兵反，隱帝遣左神武統軍袁泬、侍衛馬軍都指揮使閻晉卿等率兵拒威於澶淵。

translations.literal: Wei raised troops in rebellion. The Hidden Emperor sent Left Divine Martial Commander Yuan Gui, Palace Horse Guard Commander Yan Jinqing, and the rest to lead troops against Wei at Chanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei rebelled. The emperor sent Yuan Gui and Yan Jinqing against him at Chanyuan.

sentences.zh: 兵未出，威已至滑州，帝大懼，謂大臣曰：「昨太草草耳。

translations.literal: Before the army marched out, Wei had already reached Huazhou. The emperor was greatly afraid and told the ministers: “Yesterday we were far too hasty.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army moved, Guo Wei was already at Huazhou. The emperor was terrified and told his ministers: “Yesterday we moved too rashly.

sentences.zh: 」業請出府庫以賚軍，宰相蘇禹珪以為未可，業拜禹珪於帝前曰：「相公且為官家勿惜府庫。

translations.literal: ” Ye asked to open the treasury and reward the army. Chancellor Su Yu Gui thought it not yet permissible; Ye bowed to Yu Gui before the emperor and said: “Chancellor, for the ruler’s sake do not spare the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: ” Ye asked to open the vaults and pay the troops. Su Yu Gui hesitated; Ye bowed to him before the throne: “Chancellor, for the emperor’s sake—do not hoard the treasury.

sentences.zh: 」乃詔賜京師兵及魏兵從威南者錢人十千，督其子弟作書，以告北兵之來者。

translations.literal: ” An edict then granted ten thousand cash per man to capital troops and Wei troops south with Wei, urging their sons and younger brothers to write letters telling northern troops to come.
translations.idiomatic: ” An edict paid ten thousand cash per man to capital troops and every soldier who had followed Guo Wei south, and pressed their kin to write north and summon more men.

sentences.zh: 及漢兵敗於北郊，業取內庫金寶，懷之以奔其兄保義軍節度使洪信，洪信拒而不納。

translations.literal: When Han’s army was defeated at the northern suburb, Ye took gold and jewels from the inner treasury, hid them on his person, and fled to his elder brother Hongxin, military commissioner of Baoyi; Hongxin refused him and would not admit him.
translations.idiomatic: Han fell at the northern suburb. Ye stuffed the inner treasury’s gold into his robes and fled to his brother Hongxin at Baoyi; Hongxin turned him away.

sentences.zh: 業走至絳州，為人所殺。

translations.literal: Ye fled to Jiangzhou and was killed by men there.
translations.idiomatic: He ran to Jiangzhou and men there killed him.

sentences.zh: 聶文進

translations.literal: Nie Wenjin
translations.idiomatic: Nie Wenjin

sentences.zh: 周兵至京師，隱帝敗於北郊，太后懼，使謂文進善衛帝，對曰：「臣在此，百郭威何害！

translations.literal: When Zhou’s troops reached the capital and the Hidden Emperor was defeated at the Northern Suburb, the empress dowager was afraid. She sent word asking Wenjin to guard the emperor well. He answered: “As long as I am here, what harm can a hundred Guo Weis do!
translations.idiomatic: Zhou troops reached the capital; the Hidden Emperor fell at the Northern Suburb. The empress dowager was terrified and asked Wenjin to guard the emperor. He replied: “While I stand here, what harm are a hundred Guo Weis?

sentences.zh: 」慕容彥超敗走，帝宿於七里，文進夜與其徒飲酒，歌呼自若。

translations.literal: ” Murong Yanchao was defeated and fled. The emperor lodged at Qili. That night Wenjin drank with his followers, singing and shouting as if nothing were amiss.
translations.idiomatic: ” Murong Yanchao broke and fled. The emperor slept at Qili. Wenjin spent the night drinking with his men, singing and shouting as if the world were still whole.

sentences.zh: 明旦，隱帝遇弒，文進亦自殺。

translations.literal: At dawn the Hidden Emperor was assassinated. Wenjin killed himself as well.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Hidden Emperor was murdered. Wenjin took his own life.

sentences.zh: 後贊，兗州瑕丘人。

translations.literal: Hou Zan was a native of Xiqiu in Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zan came from Xiqiu in Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其母，倡也。

translations.literal: His mother was a courtesan.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was a singing girl.

sentences.zh: 贊幼善謳，事張延朗。

translations.literal: As a boy Zan was skilled at song and served Zhang Yanlang.
translations.idiomatic: Zan sang well from childhood and served Zhang Yanlang.

sentences.zh: 延朗死，贊更事漢高祖，高祖愛之，以為牙將。

translations.literal: When Yanlang died, Zan entered the service of the Han High Ancestor, who favored him and made him a guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang died; Zan entered the Han High Ancestor’s service. The High Ancestor favored him and made him a guard officer.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，拜飛龍使，隱帝尤愛幸之。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor took the throne, Zan was made Dragon Flight Commissioner; the Hidden Emperor cherished him above all.
translations.idiomatic: At enthronement Zan became Dragon Flight Commissioner; the Hidden Emperor doted on him above all others.

sentences.zh: 楊邠等執政，贊久不得遷，乃共謀殺邠等。

translations.literal: Yang Bin and others held power, and Zan long went without promotion. He therefore joined in plotting to kill Bin and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bin and his faction ruled; Zan languished without promotion. He joined the plot to kill them.

sentences.zh: 邠等死，隱帝悔之，贊與允明等番休侍帝，不欲左右言已短。

translations.literal: When Bin and the others were dead, the Hidden Emperor repented. Zan and Yunming took turns attending the emperor in rotation, lest anyone nearby speak ill of them.
translations.idiomatic: Bin and the rest were dead; the Hidden Emperor repented. Zan and Yunming rotated attendance at his side so no courtier could whisper against them.

sentences.zh: 隱帝兵敗北郊，贊奔兗州，慕容彥超執送京師，梟首於市。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Emperor’s army was defeated at the Northern Suburb, Zan fled to Yan Prefecture. Murong Yanchao seized him and sent him to the capital, where his head was displayed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Emperor lost at the Northern Suburb. Zan fled to Yan; Murong Yanchao captured him, sent him to the capital, and had his head hung in the market.

sentences.zh: 郭允明

translations.literal: Guo Yunming
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yunming

sentences.zh: 郭允明，少為漢高祖廝養，高祖愛之，以為翰林茶酒使。

translations.literal: Guo Yunming had from youth been a steward in the Han High Ancestor’s household. The High Ancestor favored him and made him Hanlin Commissioner of Tea and Wine.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yunming was raised a steward in the Han High Ancestor’s household. The High Ancestor favored him and made him Hanlin Commissioner of Tea and Wine.

sentences.zh: 隱帝尤狎愛之，允明益驕橫無顧避，大臣不能禁。

translations.literal: The Hidden Emperor was especially fond of him. Yunming grew ever more arrogant and reckless, and the great ministers could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Emperor doted on him. Yunming grew brazen and unchecked; the great ministers could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 允明使荊南高保融，車服導從如節度使，保融待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Yunming was sent as envoy to Gao Baorong of Jingnan, with carriage, robes, and retinue like a military governor. Baorong received him with great honor.
translations.idiomatic: Yunming went as envoy to Gao Baorong of Jingnan with the carriage, robes, and escort of a military governor. Baorong treated him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 允明乃陰使人步測其城池高下，若為攻取之計者以動之。

translations.literal: Yunming secretly sent men to pace and measure the height of the city walls, as if planning an attack, to intimidate him.
translations.idiomatic: Yunming secretly had men pace the walls and measure their height—as though planning conquest—to frighten him.

sentences.zh: 荊人皆恐，保融厚賂以遺之。

translations.literal: The people of Jing were all afraid. Baorong gave him rich bribes to send him away.
translations.idiomatic: All Jingnan trembled. Baorong paid him off handsomely to see him gone.

sentences.zh: 遷飛龍使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Dragon Flight Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Dragon Flight Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 已而李業與允明謀殺楊邠等，是日無雲而昏，霧雨如泣，日中，載邠等十餘屍暴之市中。

translations.literal: Soon Li Ye and Yunming plotted to kill Yang Bin and the others. That day, though cloudless, the sky darkened; misty rain fell like weeping. At noon more than ten corpses of Bin and the rest were loaded and exposed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye and Yunming plotted to kill Yang Bin and the rest. That day the sky blackened though there were no clouds; misty rain fell like tears. At noon a dozen corpses were hauled into the market and left on display.

sentences.zh: 允明手殺邠等諸子於朝堂西廡，王章婿張貽肅血流逆註。

translations.literal: Yunming personally killed the sons of Bin and the others in the western corridor of the court hall. Wang Zhang’s son-in-law Zhang Yisi had blood flowing upward in streams.
translations.idiomatic: Yunming himself killed Bin’s sons and the others in the western corridor of the hall. Wang Zhang’s son-in-law Zhang Yisi bled upward in streams.

sentences.zh: 隱帝敗於北郊，還至封丘門，不得入，帝走趙村，允明從後追之，弒帝於民舍，乃自殺。

translations.literal: The Hidden Emperor was defeated at the Northern Suburb. Returning to Fengqiu Gate, he could not enter. The emperor fled to Zhao Village. Yunming pursued from behind, assassinated the emperor in a commoner’s house, then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated at the Northern Suburb, the Hidden Emperor reached Fengqiu Gate but could not pass. He fled toward Zhao Village. Yunming ran him down, murdered him in a peasant house, and then took his own life.
